Candidate-voter distance and vote choice in England, 2010 (Arzheimer and Evans 2012)

Source: R/data.R
bes2010.Rd

Respondents of the 2010 British Election Study face-to-face survey in English constituencies, with the driving distance from their home to each party's candidate, whether the candidate was the sitting MP, the difference in local deprivation between the respondent's and the candidate's ward, and their feelings about the parties before and after the election (Arzheimer and Evans 2012). One row per respondent and party (Labour, Conservative, Liberal Democrat; a party whose candidate's distance is unknown is left out, so the choice sets vary).

Usage

data(bes2010)

Format

A data frame with 1,788 rows (674 respondents) and 9 variables:

id

Respondent identifier.

party

Factor: labour, conservative, libdem.

chosen

1 for the party voted for.

feeling

Feeling about the party before the election, 0 to 10.

incumbent

1 if the party's candidate was the sitting MP.

distance

Driving distance between the respondent's home and the candidate's.

deprivation

Absolute difference in the Index of Multiple Deprivation 2010 between the respondent's and the candidate's ward.

rating

Feeling about the party after the election, 0 to 10 (NA if not asked or not answered).

constituency

Constituency name.

Source

Arzheimer, K. and Evans, J. (2012). Geolocation and voting: Candidate-voter distance effects on party choice in the 2010 UK general election in England. Political Geography, 31, 301-310. doi:10.1016/j.polgeo.2012.03.004 . Data: Whiteley, P.F. and Sanders, D. British Election Study, 2010: Face-to-Face Survey. UK Data Service, SN 7529. doi:10.5255/UKDA-SN-7529-1

Provenance and terms

From the replication archive of Arzheimer and Evans (2012) at the Harvard Dataverse (hdl:1902.1/17940, version 1.0, released under CC0 1.0): the file replication.dta (md5 d82e986aef3f1389c6ee3babb0a15566). The rows are those of the archive's fourth conditional logit (replication.do, line 52), dropped as Stata's clogit drops them; the respondents' ward identifiers and the candidates' postcodes are not carried over. The survey is the British Election Study, 2010: Face-to-Face Survey (Whiteley and Sanders; UK Data Service SN 7529, doi:10.5255/UKDA-SN-7529-1 ), which the UK Data Service distributes under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; use of these data should cite it. The rebuilding script is data-raw/make_examples.R of the development repository.

See also

Other datasets: afghan_leaders, bes1987, cabinets, defection, fluvax, pa2006, pres2004, sanctions

Examples

data(bes2010)
table(table(bes2010$id))                # parties in each respondent's choice set
#> 
#>   2   3 
#> 234 440 
m <- mnl(chosen ~ feeling + incumbent + distance + deprivation | 1, data = bes2010, id = "id",
         alt = "party", ref = "labour", cluster = "constituency", se = "cluster")
summary(m)
#> Conditional logit 
#> Call: mnl(formula = chosen ~ feeling + incumbent + distance + deprivation | 
#>     1, data = bes2010, id = "id", alt = "party", ref = "labour", 
#>     se = "cluster", cluster = "constituency")
#> Alternatives: labour, conservative, libdem  (base: labour)
#> 
#> Outcome equations (alternative:term):
#>                          Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)  
#> conservative:(Intercept)  0.33298    0.14278   2.332   0.0197 *
#> libdem:(Intercept)        0.05992    0.18450   0.325   0.7454  
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Generic coefficients (alternative-specific covariates):
#>               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> feeling      0.8172822  0.0609151  13.417  < 2e-16 ***
#> incumbent    0.6457370  0.1566508   4.122 3.75e-05 ***
#> distance    -0.0060600  0.0024868  -2.437   0.0148 *  
#> deprivation  0.0003232  0.0115231   0.028   0.9776    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Standard errors: cluster. Log-likelihood -328.472 on 6 parameters, 674 cases. AIC 668.94, BIC 696.02.
## the post-election ratings as rankings (equal ratings tie)
r <- bes2010[!is.na(bes2010$rating), ]
r$rank <- stats::ave(-r$rating, r$id, FUN = function(v) match(v, sort(unique(v))))
keep <- stats::ave(r$rank, r$id, FUN = function(v) length(v) >= 2 & length(unique(v)) >= 2) == 1
mr <- rologit(rank ~ incumbent + distance + deprivation | 1, data = r[keep, ], id = "id",
              alt = "party", ref = "labour")
summary(mr)
#> Rank-ordered logit 
#> Call: rologit(formula = rank ~ incumbent + distance + deprivation | 
#>     1, data = r[keep, ], id = "id", alt = "party", ref = "labour")
#> Alternatives: labour, conservative, libdem  (base: labour)
#> 
#> Outcome equations (alternative:term):
#>                          Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> conservative:(Intercept)  0.57840    0.09077   6.372 1.86e-10 ***
#> libdem:(Intercept)        0.60976    0.09520   6.405 1.51e-10 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Generic coefficients (alternative-specific covariates):
#>               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> incumbent    0.4494021  0.0960493   4.679 2.88e-06 ***
#> distance    -0.0001369  0.0010919  -0.125    0.900    
#> deprivation -0.0079397  0.0058598  -1.355    0.175    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
